doc.title: Konitz Lee — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Sixties: Verve end, California, Half Note, Duets
title: Other duets, reception and the Japanese duet record
summary: Other duets, the five-star review, and a Japanese record with Clark Terry and Mulligan.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: For Donald Erb the composer. How did you and Joe Henderson decide on “You Don’t Know What Love Is”?
I think I sat in with his big band at the Half Note one night and we did something and decided to play that tune. Maybe that’s how.
That record kind of got you a lot of attention. You got five stars in Downbeat.
Dan Morgenstern said “If you only buy one record this year make this the one.”
He gave you a rave review and I think that’s another one of your records that’s still one of your “primo” records that still gets talked about a lot.
It’s very nice, yeah. Do you know the Japanese duet record?
That’s interesting, too. I play a free piece with Clark Terry and a free trio with Gerry Mulligan and Peggy Stern; no ego there. Gerry is just “Okay, let’s do that”, no questions asked.
Oh God, there you go with the dates again.
With Peggy it would be from the nineties because that’s when the two of you were playing together.
